I have finally gotten around to setting up a number of IP security cameras that record motion-detected video to my house server. Now, I want a way to sync (immediate) the folder to a cloud-based storage system. I remember seeing some people writing an application that will sync the files to Amazon's services as well as Google. Ideally, I'd like:

  • Unlimited storage (The software I am running is set to only store recordings for X days, so it will self-recycle)
  • Linux support to immediately detect changes and sync the video files to the cloud.
  • Bonus: Sync files as they are being written. So, if someone unplugs my server, it is uploading the partially recorded video right up until the moment it loses connectivity.

Cost is not so much a worry. Reliability, speed (I am on a gigabit fiber-optic connection) and immediate sync more so.

What are your recommendations?
Looking for a file system that syncs to cloud storage ...

If you want to sync there's so many apps out there that will do Google, Amazon, Mega, etc. I use Mega and it's pretty good, their sync client is nice. Plus you have the whole encrypted thing.

But if you want immediate/partial sync and have a fast connection, maybe you could just use an SSH mount? Any host would work, as long as you can SSH to it.

sshfs user@host.com:/folder /mnt/remote
I use Copy. But they are ending service in May. Kind of unfortunate as it was free up to 25GB and had a decent Linux client as well as having AES-256.
Owncloud has linux support. There's a french guy runs a server on openmailbox.org and charges very reasonable prices.

Set up your own server at home, then enter into a server swap agreement with a trusted friend. You and your friend each back up to the other person's server.

I use an MSI-Wind PC with a bunch of 3TB hard drives. Total power draw never exceeds 25W and the server literally cost me $45+ hard drives.
I like Dropbox. Works great on Linux. Just put a folder link from you pictures to your Dropbox folder. Done.
